event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States calls its campaign Operation Epic Fury and says it began to protect U.S. forces, regional partners and navigation; Iran has described the U.S. and Israeli actions as unlawful aggression.

facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions
facts.value: The United States notified the Security Council that it was acting in self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran has told the Council that the U.S. and Israeli campaign constituted aggression and that subsequent Iranian measures were self-defense; these are opposing state positions, not a judicial determination.

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.

explore_lenses.title: U.S. tanker strikes and reported maritime attacks
explore_lenses.summary: The U.S. military publicly confirmed strikes on five Iranian crude carriers on September 8; reports of subsequent attacks on commercial shipping are more limited and partly contested. The episode combines verified military statements with claims that have not been independently resolved.

claims.text: CENTCOM said it destroyed five Iranian crude oil carriers on September 8 after alleging that the IRGC had twice attempted to strike a U.S. Navy warship with ballistic missiles; it said the U.S. ship evaded the attacks and no U.S. personnel were harmed.
CENTCOM named four carriers struck in the Gulf of Oman and a fifth near Kharg Island, and said crews were directed to abandon ship before the vessels were rendered inoperable.
Iranian authorities said their actions were self-defence and alleged attacks on U.S. facilities and ships; CENTCOM denied that any U.S. warship had been hit.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations service reported several merchant vessels hit by disabling fire in the Northern Arabian Gulf and Gulf of Oman, but did not publicly identify the vessels or assign responsibility.

explore_lenses.summary: The immediate escalation follows a longer conflict that had disrupted Hormuz shipping and a period of reduced tensions under a U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding. The parties sharply disagree over who initiated the wider war and whether Iranian maritime restrictions are lawful or amount to a closure.

claims.text: ABC reported that a large U.S.-Israeli attack on Iran in late February was followed by Iran's near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz, helping create a prolonged supply disruption.

Al Jazeera, citing AFP and Reuters, reported that Brent's last comparable high was July 24, after a U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding had been in place and oil prices had been falling; it also reported that attacks resumed at the end of August.

A UN Security Council resolution adopted in March demanded that Iran cease attacks on Gulf states and Jordan and stressed that commercial vessels' navigational rights and freedoms must be respected.

explore_lenses.title: No announced settlement; security measures remain contingent
explore_lenses.summary: Neither side had announced a new diplomatic agreement on September 9. The concrete next steps in public view were Iranian plans for a maritime restricted area and a multinational maritime-security mission that governments describe as defensive but conditional on circumstances.

claims.text: The IRGC said it would announce coordinates for a "prohibited zone" extending from near Chabahar through parts of the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea, and said vessels entering without coordination would face Iranian sanctions.

The UK government said its planned multinational Hormuz mission would become operational when conditions allow; its announced contribution includes mine-hunting systems, counter-drone capabilities, Typhoon aircraft and HMS Dragon.
Goldman Sachs forecast that intensified attacks in the Gulf and Red Sea could push global oil prices above $120 per barrel; this is an analyst forecast, not a confirmed outcome.

story_report.summary: Twelve governments have jointly moved toward restrictions on trade linked to Israeli settlements, citing escalating settler violence, settlement expansion and E1 tenders that they say threaten a two-state outcome. The UK, France and Canada said they would introduce national bans on settlement goods, while the wider group outlined varying national or European measures. Britain also announced action against companies and individuals supporting settlement expansion. OCHA reported that more than 1,040 Palestinians were injured in settler attacks through late August 2026, including 80 incidents causing casualties or property damage during the second and third weeks of August. The International Court of Justice’s 2024 advisory opinion found Israel’s settlement policy breached the Fourth Geneva Convention, while Israel disputes descriptions of its policies as unlawful.

sections.heading: Britain's planned enforcement timetable
sections.body: The UK said its regime would apply to settlements and their expansion, rather than trade with Israel within its pre-1967 borders. It plans legislation and a sanctions regime within six to nine months, while immediately sanctioning additional extremist settlers and expanding tools to act against settlement growth. The measures would also cover companies and individuals providing construction, infrastructure, financing or real-estate services for settlement expansion.

story_report.summary: Anthropic researcher Evan Hubinger said he believes there is a greater than 10% chance that artificial intelligence could kill all humans within the next decade, a personal forecast rather than an established scientific probability. The warning has drawn added attention after colleague Jacob Coxon resigned over fears that companies are pursuing out-of-control AI. The developments have sharpened a dispute over whether rapid advances toward superintelligent systems can be made safe enough to deploy.

sections.heading: Hubinger’s Superintelligence Risk Scenario
sections.body: Hubinger said the danger does not stem primarily from present AI models, which he described as low risk. Instead, he identified a pathway in which recursive self-improvement produces superintelligence that exceeds human control. Anthropic’s April risk report said its Mythos Preview showed strong performance on some specialist tasks but was not fully reliable, and that its ability to carry out complex covert tasks reliably was limited.

sections.heading: Coxon Challenges Industry AI Race
sections.body: Coxon argues that Anthropic and OpenAI are acting irresponsibly by racing toward self-improving superintelligence. He called for stricter conditions before pursuing what he termed the industry’s “endgame,” including extraordinary confidence that safer alternatives do not exist. Hubinger, while saying Anthropic is trying its best, said the company does not have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence.

sections.heading: Anthropic Safeguards and Regulatory Proposals
sections.body: Anthropic says Mythos 5.1 is limited to vetted organizations, while a more broadly available counterpart includes safeguards limiting risky cybersecurity and biology capabilities. The company says its system cards document capabilities, safety evaluations and deployment decisions, and its risk assessment examined both a model’s potential to attempt harm and whether monitoring and security could stop it. Separately, Sky News reported that Darren Jones called for a multinational AI treaty and discussion at future G7 and G20 meetings.

unresolved.text: Hubinger’s extinction estimate is not a measured probability: it rests on contested assumptions about future AI capabilities, behavior, resource access and safeguard effectiveness. Whether recursive self-improvement would create durable harmful goals, and whether such systems could be reliably controlled, remains unresolved.

It is unclear whether Coxon’s resignation will alter Anthropic’s development plans, other companies’ practices or government policy. The supplied reporting also does not establish that a proposed treaty, law or coordinated international testing regime has been adopted.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States calls its campaign Operation Epic Fury and says it began to protect U.S. forces, regional partners and navigation; Iran has described the U.S. and Israeli actions as unlawful aggression.

facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions
facts.value: The United States notified the Security Council that it was acting in self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran has told the Council that the U.S. and Israeli campaign constituted aggression and that subsequent Iranian measures were self-defense; these are opposing state positions, not a judicial determination.

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a limited set of developments from July 22-27, 2026—military threats, congressional war-powers action, shipping and oil-market pressure, Houthi claims, and ceasefire diplomacy—not the conflict’s full origins, all operations, or its eventual outcome.

event_overview.title: About Fatal Amazon Cargo Plane Crash at Miami International Airport
event_overview.subject: Fatal Amazon Cargo Plane Crash at Miami International Airport
event_overview.summary: On September 6, 2026, a Boeing 767 cargo flight operated by 21 Air for Amazon overran a runway after arriving at Miami International Airport from San Juan, Puerto Rico. The aircraft struck ground vehicles and caught fire; five people were killed, and the crash is the subject of a federal safety investigation whose cause had not been determined as of September 8.

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: The accident occurred at about 2 p.m. local time on September 6, 2026, at Miami International Airport in Miami, Florida.

facts.label: Flight and aircraft
facts.value: FAA identified the flight as 21 Air Flight 7598, a Boeing 767-300 cargo aircraft that had departed Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico.

facts.label: Casualties
facts.value: Five people were killed after the runway overrun struck ground vehicles; authorities also reported injuries. Reporting on September 8 said those killed were occupants of a van used by plane cleaners.

facts.label: Investigation
facts.value: The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating. Its process gathers evidence before issuing a final report that determines probable cause, so early facts should not be treated as conclusions about why the crash occurred.

explore_lenses.title: A late, incomplete abort is under review
explore_lenses.summary: Preliminary information points to an attempted go-around during an unstable landing, followed by an unsuccessful effort to stop. That sequence is not a finding of cause: investigators still need cockpit-recording context and crew interviews.

claims.text: NTSB Chair Jennifer Homendy said flight data indicated the crew appeared to briefly attempt a go-around, then abandoned it and tried to stop; the data showed thrust reversers were not used.
The NTSB reported the aircraft traveled about 1,300 feet beyond the runway end; the agency's investigation page identifies the event as a runway overrun during landing on Runway 30.

Former FAA official Mike O'Donnell said the touchdown on the nose and right landing gear appeared consistent with an unstable landing and that the crew may have delayed the go-around; this is expert interpretation, not an NTSB conclusion.

story_report.summary: An Amazon cargo plane arriving from San Juan overran Runway 30 at Miami International Airport after its crew attempted to abort an unsteady landing, federal investigators said. The aircraft crashed beyond the runway, killing five people in a van used by an airline contract-cleaning service. Two other people remained in critical condition. The National Transportation Safety Board has classified the September 6, 2026, event as a runway overrun and has opened an ongoing investigation.

sections.heading: Flight Data Shows Aborted Go-Around
sections.body: NTSB Chair Jennifer Homendy said flight data indicated the crew of 21 Air Flight 7598 briefly appeared to attempt a go-around before abandoning it and trying to stop the Boeing 767. The data also showed that thrust reversers were not used. The aircraft traveled about 1,300 feet beyond the runway end, according to the NTSB. Former FAA official Mike O'Donnell said the landing appeared unstable and the go-around may have been delayed, an expert assessment rather than an NTSB finding.

sections.heading: Overrun Struck Cleaning-Service Van
sections.body: According to an NTSB account reported by Local 10, the aircraft struck navigational aids and airport equipment before hitting a seven-person van owned by Professional Ocean Service Corporation, an airline contract-cleaning company. It then breached a perimeter fence and struck an SUV on Northwest 67th Avenue. All five fatalities were occupants of the cleaning-service van; as of September 8, two injured people were in critical condition, while the pilot and co-pilot had been released from the hospital.

sections.heading: NTSB and FAA Continue Investigations
sections.body: The NTSB has deployed a go-team to investigate the Part 121 cargo flight and lists the case as ongoing. The FAA also said it would investigate the overrun. NTSB investigators were scheduled to interview the pilot and co-pilot on September 9 while examining flight-data and cockpit-voice recordings. Miami-Dade Mayor Daniella Levine Cava said the inquiry is intended to determine the cause and develop future safety recommendations, though any recommendations will depend on the evidence.

event_overview.title: About U.S.-Canada Trade War
event_overview.subject: U.S.-Canada Trade War
event_overview.summary: The U.S.-Canada trade war is an escalating bilateral dispute in which the United States has imposed additional import restrictions and tariffs on Canadian goods and Canada has responded with retaliatory tariffs on U.S. products. It developed alongside, and in some cases outside the preferential tariff framework of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA/CUSMA), with both governments citing alleged discriminatory treatment of their exporters.

facts.label: Trade-agreement context
facts.value: USMCA/CUSMA entered into force on July 1, 2020 and generally preserved zero tariffs among the United States, Canada and Mexico, although later U.S. measures covered some Canadian goods regardless of USMCA origin status.

facts.label: Early formal dispute
facts.value: Canada initiated WTO consultations on March 4, 2025 over U.S. additional duties of 25% on Canadian non-energy goods and 10% on Canadian energy goods; the United States accepted consultations on March 14 while disputing WTO reviewability of the measures.

facts.label: U.S. legal basis and 2026 tariff action
facts.value: The July 2026 U.S. actions relied on Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, which permits presidential action, including duties up to 50%, to address an unequal or discriminatory burden on U.S. commerce. The United States imposed 50% duties on covered Canadian products effective August 22, 2026 after a temporary suspension lapsed.

facts.label: Canadian countermeasures
facts.value: Canada announced retaliatory tariffs of 15%, 25% and 50% on U.S. imports worth C$27.6 billion, effective September 8, 2026, with rates intended to match corresponding U.S. Section 338 and Section 232 measures. Covered sectors include steel and aluminum, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, plastics and electronics.

facts.label: September 2026 import bans
facts.value: On September 8, 2026, the United States proclaimed import bans on specified Canadian products that had been subject to Section 338 duties; the bans are scheduled to apply to covered imports from 12:01 a.m. Eastern time on September 29, 2026.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline focuses on the late-August and September 2026 escalation—new reciprocal tariffs and announced U.S. import bans—not the full history of U.S.-Canada trade relations, USMCA disputes, or every affected product and support measure.

event_overview.title: About Syria Conflict
event_overview.subject: Syria Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Syria conflict began with protests in March 2011 and developed into a prolonged, multi-sided conflict involving Syrian state forces, armed opposition groups, Kurdish-led forces, Islamist armed groups and outside powers. The overthrow of Syria’s former government on 8 December 2024 opened a political transition, but the United Nations has continued to describe the security and humanitarian situation as volatile, including in the north-east and north-west.

facts.label: Start and current phase
facts.value: The conflict began in March 2011. After the former government was overthrown on 8 December 2024, Syria entered a transition rather than a clearly defined, universally recognized end to the conflict.

facts.label: Location and conflict character
facts.value: The conflict is centered in Syria but has had regional effects, including large-scale displacement to neighbouring countries. Armed and political control has varied across the country, with north-eastern Syria and Idlib in the north-west among areas particularly relevant to the selected developments.

facts.label: Political framework
facts.value: UN Security Council Resolution 2254 (2015) identifies an inclusive, Syrian-led political process as the sustainable route to resolving the crisis and calls for implementation of the 2012 Geneva Communiqué.

facts.label: Syrian Democratic Forces
facts.value: The Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) emerged in 2015 as a coalition including Arab, Kurdish, Christian, Syriac, Turkmen and other forces, and became a principal local partner of the United States-led campaign against the Islamic State in north-eastern Syria.

facts.label: Integration into state institutions
facts.value: On 10 March 2025, Syria’s caretaker authorities and the SDF signed an agreement envisaging integration of civil and military institutions in north-eastern Syria into the state administration; the United Nations later continued to call for implementation of that understanding.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States calls its campaign Operation Epic Fury and says it began to protect U.S. forces, regional partners and navigation; Iran has described the U.S. and Israeli actions as unlawful aggression.

facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions
facts.value: The United States notified the Security Council that it was acting in self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran has told the Council that the U.S. and Israeli campaign constituted aggression and that subsequent Iranian measures were self-defense; these are opposing state positions, not a judicial determination.

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.

event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.
